utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. I apologise for being a bit late, for practical reasons. I think before we resume with the cross-examination of the witness, I would just like to draw your attention to two issues. The first one is that no formal decision had yet been taken on the tendering into evidence of the previous statement of Witness L, although I indicated to the Prosecution that there was a fair chance that it would not be admitted into evidence. The final decision is in accordance with the indication I gave at that moment to the parties. Then a second issue: I have been rethinking what happened yesterday as far as the cross-examination was concerned about indiscriminate shooting in what army. I would just make quite clear to Mr. Piletta-Zanin that I do not oppose in any way to him putting these kinds of questions to the witness, because as far as I understood, he wanted to know whether the witness was aware of indiscriminate shooting not only in the army she referred to, the Republika Srpska army, but also in the other army. So I do not mind in whatever way that you put such a question to the witness, but I thought it was not necessary to twist the answer already given by the witness in such a way that it would seem some kind of logic. There was nothing logical in it. It was just a question on whether she thought that indiscriminate shooting perhaps would have happened also in the other army. So I do not oppose about the question; I was mainly opposing about the way in which the question was presented to the witness. Having said this, I think we could continue with the cross-examination -- Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I merely wish to inform the Trial Chamber that following the completion of the evidence of this witness, I propose to be absent during the -- at least part of the examination of the following two witnesses, if that is acceptable to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's acceptable. We have to be very careful what the other party says during your absence. As you might have noticed, I went through the transcript on that specific point. So then Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are ready to continue the cross-examination of the witness? Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Honour. I should like to take the opportunity of this short break to tell the Chamber that I will be very careful and cautious not to say anything in absence of anyone anything that might be interpreted as inadvertent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Sahic. Do you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not speak a lot of Serbo-Croatian, but "dobro jutro" is something I do understand by now. The cross-examination by the Defence will be continued. I'd just like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration as you made yesterday at the beginning of your testimony. Please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: First of all, for the benefit of the interpreters, whom I should like to thank, that if there's any problem with hearing me, please let me know. Madam, thank you for coming back to the courtroom. I should like to go back to the system which I criticized of electronically manipulated photographs. I should like to see put on the screen the same photograph that we were looking at together at the end of the last session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it please be put on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I'm concerned, I have the image on the screen. I hope everyone else does as well. May I proceed? Does the witness have the image on the screen? Thank you. For the benefit of the technical booth, could we have some panning from right to left in a circular motion, please. Thank you. And could we zoom it a little bit forward. Thank you. And a little up, yes, so that we can see the horizon. And if you would please continue panning the image. A little more. Yes. Thank you. We can stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please tell us the name of the hills that you see in the image at this moment.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is difficult for me to tell which mountain it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Let us continue, please. Good. We can stop here. But I should like to have a more -- a closer look of the photograph, to zoom backwards. I think that is the right term. Thank you. Witness, on this image, you see, I believe, a building. In the centre of the image, in the background. What is that building? Can you see a white building in the centre of the screen?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What is this building? Can you tell us about it?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the mosque at Kobilja Glava.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. On the other hand, there is a partially obscured building that we can see on the left. Is this the building in front of which you happened to be at the moment the shooting started? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It happened on this road that you can see next to the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And if my memory serves me well, you were in the immediate vicinity of this building that we can see only partially. And how many metres away from the house were you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You can see a hole on the road, and that is where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So how far from the building? How many metres from the building were you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I didn't measure the distance at that moment. It was very difficult for me to tell how far I was from this building or from the greenery here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But madam, I should like you to have a look at another photograph, which is 02151426 [as interpreted], a photograph which has been submitted by the Prosecution. Has this photograph been shown to the witness? Yes. You have a photograph in front of you, madam. There is a person shown on this photograph that you told us was your father. Is that correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you just allow me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I'm looking at the screen. I see -- I don't know whether you said it or whether it's a mistake, but it says 02151426.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I said 36.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are looking at the photo last two digits being 36. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We are talking about the same photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, you testified yesterday when talking about this photograph that at the relevant times you were standing on this particular location when the shooting started. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, you also told us that the shooting came from the area in front of you, ahead of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I should like to know something about the corner of this building that we can see on the photograph. Is that the same corner that we saw on the previous picture?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't -- I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. A moment ago you saw a computerised photograph. I know that it was not very clear, but that's how it is. And we stopped a certain point on this photograph and we were looking at the corner of a building. And I'm now asking you a question about this photograph. Two corners on these two documents, the one that you saw a moment ago and that you see here in front of you, are they the same corners of the same building?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This is not one and the same building? I should like to be perfectly clear, and let me refer myself to the translation, because the answer might be very important?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I notice that the witness is looking at the photograph on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And having regard to the way it is placed on the ELMO, I don't think it's possible in its depiction on the screen to see the building to which my friend refers. So therefore I ask that the image be replaced on the screen, or alternatively the witness look at the photo directly and that Mr. Piletta-Zanin refers her again to the corner of the building which he has in mind. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, although I think this is a good suggestion, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, to at least have the whole picture on the screen instead of just part of it. Could it be put on the ELMO in such a way? Perhaps I would prefer that, the whole picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that is one of the reasons why I objected to the use of this electronically manipulated photograph. They're very difficult to use in the courtroom. So I was referring to the computerised photograph that we saw a moment ago, and I should like to have it back on the screen and to see the same spot where we stopped before the intervention of Mr. Ierace. Could we see the electronically manipulated photograph once again, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it please be put on the video. Yes, it's there, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put on your microphone, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, you see a corner of a building here that -- and we can also see a portion of the roof. Is this portion of the building here the same as the one that we can see on photograph whose last three digits are 436?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I thought I heard you say no, but now we have received an affirmative answer. Thank you very much. Witness, how many metres or even centimetres were you away from this building at the moment the shooting started? What was the distance between you and this building?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I already answered your question. I don't know exactly what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Madam, I could perhaps ask you to help us with this problem on the photograph. You know the area and you see the photograph. Could you tell us approximately what the distance was between the corner of the building and you? Could you tell us that now by looking at the photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness either cannot or doesn't want to answer, so I will move to another question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the middle of the photograph we can see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I object to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you have a full right to ask whatever questions you want to put to the witness, but any comments, even if the witness is not answering or whether she is unwilling or not capable of doing so are not appropriate at this moment, and of course at a later stage you can give whatever comment you want during your closing statement, but not during the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let me address my apologies to the Chamber. My --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to show -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me ask another question, because my previous question remained unanswered. My question is as follows: Madam, to the left side from the position which you occupied on photograph 436, do you see a wall?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This wall was probably one metre and 50 centimetres high, more or less; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I couldn't tell you exactly, but I think that your questions are useless. They have nothing to do with the event. You're talking about a house or a wall. I mean, I don't see the connection with the events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sahic, if a question is put to you, the Prosecution, if they think that the question is of no importance whatsoever, they can object against the question. The Chamber can also ask the Defence what the relevance of the question is. But as long as the question is there and as long as the Chamber and the Prosecution have not expressed any objection as far as the relevance is concerned, I would like you to answer the question. Of course, what's in your mind about relevance, that's up to you, but I would invite you just to answer the question without commenting on the relevance of it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On the other hand, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are talking about a wall and you're talking about a wall of one metre and 50 high, so I am afraid that there might be some confusion as to what wall you -- let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I said to the left on the photograph, and as far as I'm concerned, I see only one wall on the left side. And I said that it was 1.50 metres tall, and I believe I was clear. I mentioned where it was situated on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please -- [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless we have a different photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let's first clarify. We have photograph 436. On the left-hand side of the photograph I see someone standing, and I see just a tiny, little part of a roof. I have some difficulties in locating a wall there. So would you please -- and well, the roof -- I must assume is supported by a wall which is far higher than 1 metre and 50. Could you please -- if I cannot understand what your question is, the witness might have difficulties as well. So would you please be more precise on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can perhaps check the transcript, but I can also ask the question once again. I said -- I was speaking in French - to witness's left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did now follow --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To her left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did now follow your question in French. The transcript says on the left part of the photo, and what you're saying now in French is a sa gauche. That means --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm so sorry for this. I will have to look at the translation all the time, but I'm afraid it's not possible. So I'll go ahead in French.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'll assist you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. As you have seen, I now do understand that you are putting a question about a wall that is opposite to the house, the other side of the road, well let's say the side of the road where the blue demolished car is, where, if you talk about a wall, that's stones at an elevation. I think that's what your question was about. Am I correct in understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have perfectly understood my question, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please, Ms. Sahic, the question was not about a wall of the house but was about a wall just at the other side of the road where you might see some stones. Could you then please answer the question of Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Perhaps the question could be asked again, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Would you please repeat the question about that wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I'm really sorry about having these problems in interpretation, but it requires lots of concentration on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Madam, to your left side, to my left, there is a wall on this photograph; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam, yesterday you spoke about an orchard in which you took shelter. That orchard, was it situated to my left, that is, to your left, or to your right on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'm still afraid that a lot of confusion about left and right will exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said my left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I did understand. Ms. Sahic, when you're talking about the orchard, was it at the side of the road where the blue demolished car is or was it on the other side, where the house of which the roof can be partially seen?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was above the blue destroyed car, above that little half wall from the stones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, when I'm saying to my left or to my right, but I can maybe clarify.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, would you agree with me that on your right, at the time, so where your father stands on the photograph at a short distance from you, between you and the house, were you there then?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I would like to remind you, Witness, where you were wounded at the time of the shots?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This did not happen on the road, but it was up in the orchard, but I was not wounded, but Vildana Kapur.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told me that the shots took place in the orchard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please be more precise in your questioning, since the witness has testified that the shooting started, that they were seeking shelter in the orchard. So when you're talking about the shooting, would you please indicate clearly whether you talk about the beginning of the shooting or about the moment when someone, as has been testified, was hit by a bullet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, but perhaps this happens because of the languages that I'm following.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did I understand you correctly that you said that the shots by which your friend was wounded happened in the orchard while you were in the orchard?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I give an explanation as to -- in my answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may explain what you mean.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shooting started on the road that you can see on the photograph, where there are cracks. After that, we hid in that shelter, in the orchard, where we took shelter, and Vildana Kapur was standing behind a tree, where she was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. You said that your friend Mrs. Kapur was a couple of years older than you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the sake of the transcript, as far as I understand the question, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you asked whether the witness testified that her friend was one or two years older than she was. I heard in the translation "a couple of years." Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We will check the transcript, but my recollection is that the witness said that her other Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. friend was a year or two older and that Mrs. Kapur --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said that they were one or two years older.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but Mr. Ierace is drawing your attention to the fact that there were two friends there, and we have to check carefully about which friend we're speaking now. So could you -- if the -- Mr. Ierace, did you find --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The relevant --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you assist Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. The relevant page is 2585 and there's a relevant passage at line 15 and line 23. The effect of it is that the question posed by Mr. Piletta-Zanin correctly reflects the evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your assistance. And I think the correction as far as the translation is concerned, a couple of years is one or two years older. That's what your question was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I said in French was exactly what I said, is one or two years older.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I heard the translation "a couple of years." And let me just -- but I try to follow in my right ear what you say in French and with my left ear --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I know the problem, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I have no problem. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to go back to what you were saying, you said before the interruption, you said that your friend was one or two years older than you were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How old is your friend now, Mrs. Kapur?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same, one or two years.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. My question, in French, and for the translators too: What does your friend do now? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What she is doing? I don't know what she is doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it not true to say that this person was born in 1972?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not quite sure about her date of birth. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. You said in your testimony that after the incident you went down, out of the orchard, to get some help. You went to a police station to get some help. Could you tell us where the police station was?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below this road there was a kitchen. There was -- where the policemen went to get their meals. You cannot see it on this photograph, but below there, there is a public kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So below this -- the road below is the road that you indicated. Is the road --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel repeat the name of the road.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the name of the road, Stara Cesti, the old road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You were talking about a kitchen, a canteen. I believe that's where meals were served at the time -- at meal times; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And these meal times, in general and in Sarajevo as well, were, for instance, lunch-time, around noon; and in the evening, about 1800 hours, 1900 hours. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, when I went down for help, I don't know whether they were having their lunch or whether they were having -- whether they were on a break or whether they were just sitting, but that was the first building I could get to to get some help. I was not paying attention as to whether they were having their meal or whether they were on a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But Witness, you said there were a number of people in uniforms there at the time. Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were policemen. These were not soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I stand to be corrected --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't recall the witness saying that there were a number of people in uniforms, and if that --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not answer, but that was exactly the point of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Ierace, your objection was that you did not hear the witness say anything about people present in uniform; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then, please, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, indicate where the witness testified, as you put to her -- you said that there were a number of people in uniform there at the time; is that so? That was your question. Would you please indicate where the witness testified that there were a number of people in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. The witness never used the term "uniform," but she did use the term "policemen." So I believe that the point of my question would be whether these people were in uniform or not, but I suppose that would be in the interest of finding out the truth, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you then please refer to her answer ask whether these policemen were in uniform or not. I mean, if that's what you want to know. Don't talk about uniforms as if the witness has testified -- had testified before that there were people in uniforms. I know that it's an important issue for the Defence whether official people on duty are wearing uniforms or not. So if you take your own point seriously, you should do the same in questioning the witness. And I think the witness answered your question or did not answer your question, because she said that there were police people there. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, in fact, the answer replied, but in French my question was very clear. It was about men in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You said that these were police officers, so there goes a question. So why would you make a distinction between these police officers? How could you tell that they were police officers?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I saw two people in front of the canteen. They were in civilian clothing. And I called them to help us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, how did you know that these people were police officers?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because nobody else was allowed to go into that canteen except for the police officers, these people were not on duty. They were standing in front of the canteen. I did not ask them who they were, what they were doing there. I just asked them for help. I believe that is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were these people in front? There were two of them. Were there other people there who helped you?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, so according to your recollection, there were two people who helped you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the distance between the canteen and the spot that you were at on the photograph ending in numbers 1436?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the distance was, but I think it can be seen on the photograph. It was behind this house, while we were in the orchard. And I think it can be seen on the photograph. I cannot tell you exactly, because I did not measure the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What you mean to say is that the canteen can be seen on the photograph? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Below the house it can be seen in the background.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So is that also along the axis of the shot?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was below this road.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But in relation to the path of the bullet, where were you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to that question, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- in terms of clarity.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from the objection, the witness does not understand your question. Could you please rephrase it in such a way that the witness does understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will repeat it, Witness. So we will try to do it logically. Could we have the photograph 1436 on the ELMO, please. Witness, could you indicate for us on this photograph by showing -- pointing with your finger where approximately this canteen was.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below this house.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you show it? Could you point it?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot be seen. It is below.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, clearly we will not -- thank you. It's being done now.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Below this house that you can see in the background, just a little below. So you cannot see it. I cannot explain it if I can't see it. I think it's enough that I said where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for this answer. But Witness, the shots, could you tell us on this photograph where the shots were coming from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do apologise for interrupting my friend, but I suggest that for the sake of the transcript there be some description as to which house it was the witness just pointed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. For the clarity of the transcript, I'll say that the witness just pointed to the house which is seen in the middle of the photo, a little bit to the right of the head of the witness as she appears on the photograph. It's a house. The lower part is white, the upper part is wooden, and you see a brown roof. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you please indicate with a pointer the direction from which the shots were coming from. Could you tell us just with a gesture, without marking it.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The direction cannot be shown because exactly the way I am standing on the photograph and watching the camera, that's where the shots were coming from. So everything that you can see on the photograph is -- so everything is in front of me. So the shots were coming from the front, from the direction where the photographer was standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, therefore, if I tell you that the canteen was in the path of the shots, is that correct? Do you think that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The question purports to reflect the evidence of the witness so far. I don't know what word my friend used in French, but "path" is clearly inconsistent with that evidence, given the position of the house in relation to the canteen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to say once and for all that these terms that I am using are -- usually I am talking about "axe" in French, and that is a path of the bullet, and I'm going to re -- I'm going to ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So was your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will not allow you to ask the question again, since the objection has been sustained, and as far as I noticed your explanation of the word "axe" in French, and when I hear how Mr. Ierace uses the word "path," the objection is still totally valid that it does not reflect the evidence in the testimony of the witness. So put whatever other question you would like in order to find out precisely, but in your question there was an incorrect reflection of what the testimony was about. So you may not put the same question in a similar way again, but any other question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I'm going to ask a different question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'm sorry. So the canteen -- was the canteen -- were the shots in respect of the canteen roughly on the same direction of the shots?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The canteen was below the line of the shots, so that was below the road. We were being shot at and we were on the road, and the canteen was below the road. I believe that is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you an additional question, Ms. Sahic? You have explained to us a few times that the canteen was below the house which is at the side of the road. Could you please indicate to us, was this 5 metres below, 10 metres below, 20 metres below? Could you give us an indication of the difference in height between the house and the canteen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is about a floor lower, but they were about -- next to each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And do I understand from your answer that the canteen was quite close to the house you just indicated on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said yesterday that you were able to see the front lines, and in particular, the Serb front lines; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could I conclude, then, in front of these blinds there were front lines of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Were there no lines of the Bosnian army in front of the Serb lines, of the lines of the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So it was an unopposed front line?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a photograph where I can tell you exactly where the shots came from and what that place was called, and I can show you exactly in order to clarify my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I did not get an answer, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Sahic, Mr. Piletta-Zanin was asking you whether there were any front lines opposing the Serbian front lines, so front lines from the Bosnia-Herzegovinian army, opposed to the front lines of the Serb army. Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do understand the question, but these lines, these positions, could not be seen from the spot where I'm saying that the Serb lines could be seen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the first question was whether there was such an opposed line opposed to the Serbian army at the Bosnia-Herzegovinian side, whether you could see it or not at that time is a different issue, but are you aware of a front line of the Bosnia-Herzegovinian army opposing the front line of the Serbian army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said a moment ago that there were two police officers who were standing in front of the canteen, and these policemen did not -- they did not wear any specific insignia.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: They were in civilian clothing?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: These policemen who were in civilian clothing, did they have a belt for side arms?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And you are emphatic on that point?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. I did not see anything of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you see in that area - and I am referring to the time when this gunfire happened - in 1993, did you see in that area any soldiers who would be present in that area?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not see anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you saw nothing of that sort throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did see the military. They were all over. But at that particular point in time, I did not see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you say that they were all over, could you clarify what you've just said, please.

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's only natural. It was wartime and you could find military soldiers everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And by this you mean in the village too?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, yes, everywhere. I did not count them, nor did I try to establish where every one of them was. But it was wartime and there was soldiers everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Who were hiding everywhere; is that how I should interpret your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what they were doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I object to that question. The question was: Who were hiding everywhere; is that how I should interpret your testimony? The question -- the evidence of the witness was not even remotely to the effect that they were hiding everywhere, and I --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I noticed that during the last one minute you repeatedly seemed to twist the answer of the witness in order to put a quasi-logical next answer to her. For example, I'm referring to the question where you said that: You're referring to the time when this gunfire happened, did you see in that area any soldiers? The answer was: I could not see anything like that. And then your next question was: "So you saw nothing of that sort throughout the war?" I find it unacceptable that while you question the witness, you point at a certain period of time. And if the witness answered that question in relation to that specifically asked period of time, that in your next question you say, "So you were not seeing," and then referring to the whole wartime. This is not leading; this is misleading. And I will not accept that any more. I hope I'm quite clear to you. I'll give you full opportunity to cross-examine the witness. I'll not give you an opportunity to create confusion where there's no reason for that. And you might have noticed that if confusion is the result of your line -- of your way of questioning, that I will take over, which of course might lose -- might create some loss of effectivity of your cross-examination, but it's in your own hands. As the Rules say, the mode of questioning is controlled by the Chamber. I hope that I'm clear enough, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, but if my questions were interpreted in that manner, that was not my intention. But I will -- but I will take care. Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from that completely different issue, we have some arrangements as far as time is concerned. I would like to remind you of that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, another question: You told us that with your sister, you lived in that house for the duration of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And in comparison with the whole period of the war that you speak about, if I may ask you that, there were quite a number of military in that area, weren't there?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only there. There were military, there were soldiers everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So at some point -- or rather, you saw those troops. What kind of weapons would they be carrying when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you, really, what kind of -- what did they carry, what did they do, where did they go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Last question: To your knowledge, and covering the whole period that we're talking about, did it ever happen that those troops used this Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. canteen which you pointed at and told us that it was below the house which can be seen in the photograph?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that it was a police canteen, not an army canteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Is there any need for re-examination of the witness on the Prosecution side?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just in relation to one issue, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: You were asked a number of questions about the age of Vildana Kapur. For what period of time had you known her when this occurred, when the shooting occurred?

utterances.speaker: IFETA SAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not very long. Two, three years maybe. I didn't know her. I hadn't known her before that too long.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ierace. Any questions from my colleagues? Ms. Sahic, since the Bench has no questions to you, as you might have noticed, we did put some questions to you during the examination by the parties- this ends your examination as a witness. We know that it's a far way to come to The Hague, and I'm sure you understand that the information witnesses give to this Court are of great importance for the decisions we'll have to take. We thank you for coming this far way to The Hague, and I wish you a good journey home. Thank you very much. Mr. Usher, would you please lead Ms. Sahic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This brings us to the technical issues. What we have to be tendered into evidence is we have the 360-degree photographs, two of them, under one exhibit number; one photo with the centre of the road, the other one with the centre in the orchard, and that would be 3279A, if I'm correct, Madam Registrar. I'm making a mistake, as far as I -- could you please -- the 360-degree photograph from two different --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Am I correct in understanding, Mr. Ierace, that 3279A, which is 360-degree quick-time movie showing sniping incidents contains all of the 360 -- yes, I do see that it's the same number. This would also mean that since the CD has admitted -- has been admitted into evidence, of course this would only be done in as far as it has been shown. So although we do not need a specific decision on that, I'll indicate at the end of each testimony that this part of the CD-ROM is part of the evidence admitted, since of course there must be a fair opportunity for the Defence to object against any part of this CD-ROM. So as far as 3279A relates to the testimony of Witness Sahic and contains a 360-degree picture of the specific spot where that incident she testified about happened, it's part of the admitted evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The CD contains four 360-degree photographs. That's the photograph for Incident 4, the photograph for Incident 14, and two photographs for this incident, which is number 9. And might I respectfully suggest that referring to the tracks by the scheduled incident number might be an appropriate way to do it when we move on to other scheduled sniping incident evidence, there will be different CDs. Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's part of the admitted evidence by now. And we also have P3279C, which is a set of two photos with both first part of the numbers 0215, the second part of one photo -- of the number of one photo is 1436 and the other one is 1439. That's, then, admitted into evidence as well. I think, Madam Registrar, that's all we had as exhibits at this moment. Then I think the Prosecution could call its next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The next witness will be taken by Daryl Mundis, and pursuant to what I said earlier, would you, Mr. President, and Your Honours, excuse me. I will probably re-attend the Trial Chamber shortly after the end of the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis. Mr. Usher, could you please bring in the witness. Mr. Mundis, it will be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sabri Halili, Your Honour

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the Defence, this witness will be testifying with respect to scheduled sniping incident number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, can you hear me in a language which you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration at the beginning of your testimony. The text of this declaration will be given to you by the usher. Would you please make that declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Halili. Please be seated. You will first be examined by Mr. Mundis of the Prosecution. Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If I could just ask the usher when he's finished getting the water, if he could move the ELMO back slightly so I can see the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course..

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, for the record could you please state your full name and spell your last name please.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Sabri, S-a-b-r-i, and my last name, Halili, H-a-l-i-l-i.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, could you please provide your date of birth and the place where you were born, please.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The 13th of April, 1957, Vucitrn, in Kosevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Halili. During the war that broke out in Bosnia, can you tell us, please, not your street address but the city where you were living when the war broke out in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And throughout the duration of the war, did you continue to live in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what was your occupation when the war broke out in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: A member of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, did you remain a member of the army throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, in which army were you a soldier?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the course of the war, can you tell the Trial Chamber whether or not you were married?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I got married in 1992, in July.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, did you, during the duration of the war, live with your wife in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did anyone else live with you and your wife during the course of the war in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Until 1993, that is, until the 27th of June, my mother-in-law lived with us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, what was your mother-in-law's name?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Almasa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And her family name?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Konjhodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you describe for the Trial Chamber what happened on 27 June 1993?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Between half past 8.00 and 9.00 in the morning, we set off for the post office, to my mother-in-law. Because when the war broke out in Bosnia-Herzegovina, she moved to sleep in the post office building --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: -- because of the dangers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: First of all, when you say "we set off," can you please tell the Trial Chamber whom you referred to when you said "we."

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I and my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And your wife's name?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Milada.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And sir, you've testified that your mother-in-law moved to sleep in the post office building. Can you tell the Trial Chamber where your mother-in-law was working when the war broke out?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: In the post office.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us why precisely she decided to move in to the post office, to sleep in the post office?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Because of the danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay, sir. You've testified that between half past 8.00 and 9.00 in the morning you set off with your wife to the post office. Can you tell the Trial Chamber why you went with your wife to the post office on that morning, please.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: We went to the post office building because the daughter-in-law of my late mother-in-law was also killed in the war, or rather, the brother's wife. So the sister-in-law of my mother-in-law was killed, about a year earlier, and it was a year, so it was the anniversary of her death, and she decided to go and be with her brother on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me see if I understand you correct, sir. Your mother-in-law had a brother; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that brother's wife had been killed in the early stages of the war; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on this occasion, on 27 June 1993, when you and your wife went to collect your mother-in-law, that was the first anniversary of the death of your mother-in-law's brother's wife?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, you could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how long did it take you and your wife on that morning to walk from your apartment to the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Some ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And approximately how far is it from the PTT building to the house of your mother-in-law's brother, where you were going that day? How far is that distance?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, the route that we took, it's about eight kilometres, because we practically went all around the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What would be the most efficient way or the most efficient distance? You say you had to go around. What would be the straightest distance between those two buildings?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Three kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, what was the reason why you had to take a longer and more circuitous route to get to your mother-in-law's brother's house?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: We could not take a shorter route because of the snipers and barricades on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware at that time, on that day, that there were snipers in the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, how did you know that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, it was common knowledge. The whole city knew it and the media spoke about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, the areas that you were walking through, that is, the area from the PTT building to the mother-in-law's brother's house, which military force controlled the area that you were walking through?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, on the day in question, approximately how long did it take you to walk the eight kilometres to your mother-in-law's brother's house?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: About an hour and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately what time did you arrive at the mother-in-law's brother's house?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Half past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. This might be an appropriate place to take our break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I can imagine that you'd rather not enter into a new subject. Mr. Halili, you've been here only very short until now. We'll have a break and then we'll continue after the break. Yes. We'll then adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, please proceed with the examination of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, when we took the recess, I believe you had just testified that the three of you, that is, your wife, your mother-in-law, and yourself, had arrived at her brother's house at approximately half past 10.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And approximately how long did the three of you remain at your mother-in-law's brother's house?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Close to 12.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is, you departed close to 12.00; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So you were there approximately one hour and 30 minutes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during that one hour and 30 minutes that you were there, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: We sat down, had a cup of coffee, talked. Yes, we also had lunch there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then at approximately 12.00 noon on the 27th of June, 1993, the three of you - that is, yourself, your wife, and your mother-in-law - departed that house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What location was your intended destination when you departed?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: We wanted to go back home.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was your mother-in-law intending to go back to the home you shared as well or was she going to go back to the PTT building where she had been staying?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: To the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say, then, that your wife and you were escorting your mother-in-law back to the PTT building and then you and your wife would return to your home?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you departed, you've testified earlier about taking a circuitous route to get to the brother's house. Did you again take a circuitous route back to the PTT building or a direct route back to the PTT building?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: We went the same way back, that is, the circuitous route.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber what happened during the time you were escorting your mother-in-law back to the PTT building.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. After we left her brother's house and reached the vicinity of the Marsal Tito barracks, a bullet was shot at that moment. It went through the air, and my mother-in-law was very frightened. She was all of a sudden off balance and she lost one shoe. She tripped. And I told her not to be afraid, because I thought that we were not being targeted; it was -- the bullet was flying much too high. I helped her get up, and she put on her shoe and we continued. But we walked only for about ten metres when a second bullet was shot, and that bullet shot her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, when you say "that bullet shot her," can you tell us what that bullet hit or impacted?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: It hit her. It cut her artery. That's what the doctors said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When your mother-in-law was struck by this bullet, did you see any physical indications of where on your body she was struck by the bullet?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see her. At that moment I turned around, and when I turned back I saw that there was a pool of blood underneath her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like now, if you can, to the best of your recollection, to describe in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, Mr. President, for the transcript, that is, I think that line 14, page 37, that there is a mistake, that there is an error in the words uttered by my learned colleague. I don't think I heard "your body," but everything is possible, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe I said her body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Her body, yes. It's clear that you intended to say her body. Thank you for your assistance, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. It's a clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It must have been a mistake. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, if you can, please, to the best of your recollection, I would like you to describe exactly what happened when you arrived at the corner. You can begin by indicating to the best of your recollection the intersection where you were when this incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes. I think I can remember. Are you referring to the first bullet that was fired or the second one? I didn't understand what you meant, which one you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's begin with the first bullet. Do you recall approximately what intersection or what street you were on or the buildings that were nearby? Can you describe where physically you were when you heard the first bullet fired?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. Right at the beginning of the intersection, near the traffic lights.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know the name of the street or the cross street where you were when you heard that shot fired?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I believe the name of the street is Kranjcevica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall any of the buildings or other landmarks that were at that location when you heard the first shot fired?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. There were some containers there that had been put up as a shelter, as a protection. There was a building on one side, and on the other side was the Marsal Tito barracks. Opposite from the Marsal Tito barracks there were some regular, ordinary buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall in September of 2001 providing a statement to an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor at the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall during the course of that interview if the investigator asked you to mark a diagram of where you were when these shots were fired?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would ask that Exhibit P3262 be shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, I would ask you to look at the lower right-hand corner of the document that's been placed on the ELMO next to you and indicate whether or not that is your signature.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The diagram in front of you has markings both in blue ink and in black ink. Did you place all of the markings on this document or only the blue markings, or only the black markings?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The picture is not very clear, but I can see both colours, and as Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. far as I can see, there's no difference. But I don't think I can explain what exactly it was that I marked here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also can look at the original, which is at the right-hand side of you on this machine. So if that's clearer to you, especially as far as the colours are concerned.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Oh, yes. I can see now. Now it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Halili, can you please look at the map on the ELMO machine to your right and tell the Trial Chamber the colour of the markings that you personally made on the document in front of you.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The black ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is it correct to state that the investigator who interviewed you on that day made the markings that are in blue?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: It's possible, yes. I only marked, actually drew the container and the crosses, and also the arrows, number 1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is, the markings on this document that are in black ink, you made those; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Does this document, P3262, illustrate to the best of your recollection the intersection as it was on 27 June 1993 when you and your wife and mother-in-law were at this intersection?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, if you would, please look at the three Xs next to the arrow on the upper right portion of the diagram that are marked in black. Do you see those three Xs next to the arrow?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what those three Xs next to the arrow represent?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The three of us and the location where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what does the arrow represent?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The direction we were walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And approximately where on this diagram were the three of you standing or moving when you heard the first shot fired?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: We were standing where the arrow is, that is, slightly behind the arrow and the three Xs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, there are several rectangle and square-shaped objects that you marked in black on the diagram with the word "prikolica" next to them. Can you tell the Trial Chamber what those drawings represent?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: These rectangles represent the containers, and the word "prikolica" means a trailer. That is where the trailer was. It was slightly higher than the containers and it was a metre and a half up above the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's start, please, with the containers. Can you describe for the Trial Chamber what type of containers these were?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The normal metal containers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are these the type of containers that are routinely used in shipping, for example, on ships and on trucks that travel on the highways?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know the approximate size, that would be the length, height, and width of these containers?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: They were two metres or slightly over two metres high, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And approximately how long was each container?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I would say three to four -- two, three, four, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you've testified that approximately in the middle, based on the diagram, approximately in the middle of this row of containers there was a trailer. Can you describe that in a little more detail, please.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. The trailer was slightly higher than the containers and it was above the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is to say from the bottom of the trailer to the ground, there was a space?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, there are also three circles in black ink on P3262 with numbers inside the circles. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what those circles and corresponding numbers relate to shall please.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The circle number 1 indicates the spot where my late mother-in-law was standing; number 2 is me. That's where I was. And number 3, my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And these would be the locations where the three of you were standing when your mother-in-law was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please describe for the Trial Chamber how it is that your wife, indicated by the circle with the number "3" in it, was ahead of your mother-in-law and yourself.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: When the first bullet was fired, she ran. She was ahead of us. She had already crossed the intersection and she was waiting for us at the spot indicated with number 3." She was at that moment facing us, looking at us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Based again on the two circles with the numbers "1" and "2" inside of them, what was your location? How close to your mother-in-law were you when she was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Approximately half a metre, not more than that. Half a metre. I'm sorry. I cannot remember exactly, but half a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the time when you and your mother-in-law were crossing this street, did you have any type of physical contact with her as you were crossing the street?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't understand what you mean by "physical contact."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you touching your mother-in-law as the two of you crossed the street?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, for as long as we were walking towards the spot that is indicated here, she was holding me by my arm, but then she moved away.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And approximately what was the distance, if you recall, between your mother-in-law and the containers or the trailer as you walked across the street?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: One metre, one metre and a half maximum. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you have any knowledge or any idea where -- from which direction the bullet came which struck your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: From our left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That would be again looking at P3262, on the opposite side of the containers and trailer, as depicted on that diagram?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have again, as with the other witnesses, prepared a video and 360-degree scene, and I would ask that the video be shown to the witness at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, that video is P3280C.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: INVESTIGATOR: Would you please stand at the spot where you remember, to the best of your ability, the first anti-sniping barricade started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I will now mark this location using yellow spray paint. Mr. Halili, would you please indicate by pointing the direction in which you and your family were walking that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: Will you please stand in the location, the spot, where you remember, to the best of your recollection that your mother-in-law was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I will now mark this location with "X" with yellow spray paint. Would you now please stand in the spot where you were standing when your mother-in-law was shot

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I will now mark this with an "X" with the number "1" beside it. Will you now please stand in the spot where you remember the barricade that consisted of a trailer, where it started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I see you indicating two spots. Could you stand in the first spot and then we will mark the second spot as well .

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I will mark this with a line and the number "2" beside it. And the next spot where did the others -- indicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates] INVESTIGATOR: I will mark this with a line with the number "3" beside it. Now we'll make our way back to the curb. One more -- one more question, please, Mr. Halili.
