Can you please indicate from which direction you heard the shot coming at the time your mother-in-law was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, do you recall the events on the day that were videotaped on the tape that you were just shown?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes. I remember. I believe it was in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you recognise yourself in that videotape?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And to the best of your recollection, was the information that you provided to the investigator correct and accurate?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask at this time, Your Honour, that the witness be shown what's been marked as P3271, two photographs. I would ask that the first of those photographs, which bears ERN number 02114265 be placed on the ELMO next to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, again, during the course of one of the interviews by an investigator from the Office of the Prosecutor, were you shown this photograph? It's on the machine to your right.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you make any markings on that photograph with a red pen?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber what those red markings indicate?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: It's the intersection where my mother-in-law was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. And the red --

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: And the containers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Witness, in the lower left-hand corner of P3271 there are what appears to be two roofs, tiled roofs. Do you see those two roofs?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you know what those building or buildings are, can you please tell the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: These are the buildings -- you mean houses, these family, private houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm talking about the roofs in the lower left-hand corner of the picture, if you know what building or buildings that is, if you could please identify that for the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The houses where --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter did not hear the witness's last few words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer, Mr. Halili, because the interpreters could not clearly hear you. Perhaps you could adjust the microphone so that -- Mr. Usher, if you could assist Mr. Halili so that it's ... Please could you then repeat your last answer. The question was about whether you could identify the houses in the lower left corner of the photograph. I think these are the roofs with a lot of small chimneys on it, two red roofs.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: These are houses that were near the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Halili?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would now ask that the witness be shown the second photograph that is part of P3271, the photograph bearing ERN number 02114266.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Halili, when you were interviewed by the investigator from the --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I have ERN 02114267 as the second photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We see, as a matter of fact, that there are two different numbers on it. There's a red number which is stricken out, as far as I can see, and we have a black number on the top and just the last digit of the stricken out right number is 7 and the black on the top indicates that the last digit is 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. I was referring to the black number at the top of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask the Prosecution to -- not to put too many numbers of photographs which might be confusing now and then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, during the time that you met with the investigator in 2001, did you also view this photograph which is now to your right on the ELMO machine?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you make any markings on this photograph with a red pen?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I put a circle around the -- around the skyscraper.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And why did you put a circle around the skyscraper?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: That was the direction where the bullet had come from, from that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in the lower right-hand portion of this photograph, there appear to be one or perhaps two buildings in the bottom right-hand side of the photograph. Do you know what that building or buildings are?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The barracks, former barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That would be the Marsal Tito barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you happen to know where the confrontation lines were between the army of the BH and the VRS on the 27th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I do know. The Miljacka River was a line of separation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at the time when your mother-in-law was shot, on which side of that line were the three of you located?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: On the side of the BH army, on our territory. On the territory under the control of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the white skyscraper that's been circled in photograph 4266, on which side of the confrontation line was that building located?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: On the other side of the Miljacka River.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is it possible to indicate on this photograph approximately where the Miljacka River is located?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, possibly about 10, 15 metres from the skyscraper. There's a promenade which is between the river and the skyscraper

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In the middle of the photograph, towards the bottom, there are what appear to be some trees. Do you see those trees?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Are these trees located near the Miljacka River?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, let me return to the immediate moments after your mother-in-law was shot. Do you recall what happened once you saw the blood, the pool of blood that you indicated was next to her?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. At that moment I went to her. I took her under her arms and I pulled her behind this wheel of that trailer that was standing there so that we could take cover, both of us, from the bullets. Because I presume there could be more coming, so that they wouldn't hit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Approximately how long did you remain behind the wheel of that trailer.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: A few seconds, because at that moment a white vehicle arrived. And when they saw that a woman was shot, they let us put her in the vehicle. So -- and then another vehicle arrived, another Golf vehicle arrived, and then we took her to the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was the first vehicle? You said a white vehicle. What type of vehicle was that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: It was a Golf.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who got into that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: My wife, my mother-in-law, and there was a driver. And as far as I can remember, there was a co-driver in the vehicle as well. There were two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And then you've testified a second Golf arrived. Who got into that vehicle?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I went in and I asked the young man -- in fact, he offered himself to take me to the hospital so that I could see what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you in fact go to a hospital?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Which hospital did you go to that day?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Military hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with any medical personnel at the hospital that day in relation to your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: At that moment when I entered the hospital, at the entrance to the hospital I saw that there was a cable, and my mother-in-law was lying there and they had cut her dress. And they asked me, "What are you doing there?" So I said that I was a son, but they threw me out. And I saw that my mother-in-law was covered in blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not quite sure from the transcript. It indicates "a cable".

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, when you arrived at the hospital, you indicated -- you testified that your mother-in-law was lying there. Upon what was your mother-in-law lying?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: In an operating theatre, on a bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the doctors -- or did a doctor or doctors later indicate to you what had happened to your mother-in-law?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes. A doctor came and said -- he offered his condolences and said that he was sorry, but that she was dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did the doctor indicate to you what the cause of death was?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did the doctor tell you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: He said that she had been shot with a defragmentation bullet, and he showed the bullet and said that had killed her.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, do you recall what type of clothing you were wearing on the day your mother-in-law was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. I had black trousers and a black shirt with white stripes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was this black trousers and black shirt with white stripes part of a military uniform?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No. This was my own clothes, my civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on this day when your mother-in-law was shot, were you carrying any kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No, I did not, because there were not enough weapons to go around, not even for standing guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And at the time when the shot was fired that struck your mother-in-law, did you see any soldiers in the immediate vicinity?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you see any military equipment of any kind in the immediate vicinity at the time your mother-in-law was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what type of clothing your mother-in-law was wearing the day she was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: She had a red dress on, and it had a print of a tiger on the front. And she was wearing a large woman's belt around her waist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what type of clothing your wife was wearing on that day?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the approximate age of your mother-in-law at the time she was shot?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, Mr. Halili, was your mother-in-law in the military at the time she was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, Mr. Halili, was your mother-in-law ever in the military during the course of her life?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Finally, I would like to show the witness the 360-degree panorama photo, which is also contained on P3279A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, do you recognise the image that's on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what this image depicts.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: You can see the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Would this be the Marsal Tito barracks?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the photo be slowly panned to the left, please. Pause, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, does this view indicate the intersection where your mother-in-law was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask if the photo could be slightly tilted downwards. Thank you. And if it can then be zoomed in, please. Further. Further. All the way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that there might be a technical problem at this moment. Could we just wait, because it was not ordinary zooming in, as far as I noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As Mr. Piletta-Zanin also noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think it was obvious to us all, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll get a message when the problem is solved. How much time it will take is not clear to me, but I see that we've now different pictures, at least my left neighbour has a different picture on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Unfortunately, Mr. President, I'm in my final few questions and I think they're going to require the use of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then we'll have to wait for a second, unless it would take really a considerable period of time. Then I would suggest that we -- Madam Registrar. It's on the screen, yes. So could you please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If the technician could please pan the photo slightly to the right. Stop, please. Slightly down. Stop, please. And slightly zoom in, please. That's fine. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, can you see in the centre of the video that is now before you a white skyscraper?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is that the same building that you circled on P3271, the second page, marked 4266?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If the photo can please be zoomed back and panned to the left. Please stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, do you see a police vehicle in the centre of the photo or the video that's on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is that police vehicle in the approximate location where the three of you were standing when you heard the first gunshot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please continue panning to the left. Stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The street that is immediately in the centre of the photograph, which extends into the distance, that is would be towards the rear of the photograph, do you see that street?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, was this the street that you were walking down with your wife and mother-in-law prior to arriving at the intersection where she was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Please continue panning to the left. You can stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, does this electronic photograph correctly convey, to the best of your knowledge, the intersection where your mother-in-law was shot?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Halili.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecutor has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Is the Defence ready to cross-examine the witness? Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely, Mr. President. Thank you. I was just going to get organised. Perhaps we could know when the next break will be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next break will be, as usual, at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for being here. I would like to go back to what you have just told us. First of all, in relation to a date that was mentioned by the Prosecution, which is the 27th of June, 1993, you confirm this date, do you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I heard the Prosecution ask you a question in respect of military equipment. In this area, and on that day, could you confirm what I don't believe I heard, that there was no combat ongoing on that day and in that area.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No, there weren't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us, sir, and we saw it on the computer electronically, although there were certain problems, that the intersection was close to the barracks, to the Marsal Tito barracks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Is it true -- just to check it. Is it correct to say that you were an army man?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I was. That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, at the time when the incident that we are talking about happened, were you a soldier still?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, but I was having a day off, because how we worked was to stand guard for 48 hours and then be free for 48 hours, and that was one of my days off.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But you were nevertheless a member of the army, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. You mentioned a moment ago, clearly, that shots were fired.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I said two shots.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That's right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have a technical problem. I'd like to show the witness a document which is in English. So that I should also like to give it to the interpreters so that they could interpret the passage I require. Do I have your leave to do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is this a document known to the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As it frequently happens, Mr. President, it is a document which was supplied by the Prosecution. The number is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Yes, the number is?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ERN 0093254. So 3254.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please provide the interpretation booth with a copy as well, and then ... Do you intend to tender this document into evidence, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would then --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We intend to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You know, one of the arrangements is that parties will prenumber --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it would be possible for the Prosecution to get a copy of this document, we would greatly appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would there be an additional copy for the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be happy to give the Prosecution my copy. Yes, I shall be very happy to do that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, now we have this technical difficulty that we have to cope with, because the interpreters in B/C/S will need to follow my question, because I will be asking the witness to confirm what I will tell him, or evidently say that that is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to begin with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin: If you are referring -- because you gave an English text to the witness, which I assume he cannot read. Do you read any English?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is what I was going to ask the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I don't think you can read English; however, you will tell me now if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I can read English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You do read English. Well, then I shall be very happy to -- will you please take up this document which you have in front of you, please, and will you please then confirm for me what it says here as for the date, for the period -- which the period is under consideration, the date which is two on the -- excuse me - right-hand side of the document, in the penultimate box, in this square that you have before you. Which is the date?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: 27th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that the figures 00 -- 0001, and then 2359, mean that this covers the whole day, the whole of the 27th of June, that is, from the first minute of that particular day to the last minute of that same day?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Excuse me. Why, yes, the 27th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you please then look at page 2 of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, it is the same document, but the end figures are 255.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you see item 1, that is, number 1 in brackets on this page?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, Witness, what does the word "EgyBat" mean?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could it mean the acronym for the Egyptian battalion present in Sarajevo at the time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution objects, Your Honour. The witness has said he doesn't know what that term means, number 1; and number 2, I'm not sure if the Defence has laid a proper foundation for establishing if this witness would have any particular knowledge that would be probative on this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be happy to help my learned friends, and I'm moving directly to my next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, will you please -- will you please read what we see under number 3 in brackets on this page 2, if you can.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, but will you please do that aloud.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: UkrBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I meant the whole sentence, Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: "UkrBat".

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear that, but UkrBat is one word?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the witness was concentrating to start reading the rest of the line. A bit of patience might not be bad. Could you please read those three lines following number 3 which start with "UkrBat," at least if you're able to pronounce the English words, because you told us that you could read them. Could you please try to -- I'll -- if it's just a matter of reading, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since the witness seems to have some difficulties, I'll read it aloud: "UkrBat during the reported period the situation was relatively tense due to SA fire and RT shelling in the vicinity of Tito barracks." Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President, for your help.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm speaking in principle that the abbreviation "SA" could perhaps mean small arms. Could you confirm this, since you are a military man?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a United Nations document. In terms of a variety of foreign militaries are represented here and there's no -- there's been no showing, no foundation laid that this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall move on to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, you have heard the interpretation of this sentence. Did you understand it?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Then I will once again ask for the interpreters to assist me and ask you to interpret -- translate the sentence for you, because the witness did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could you perhaps read it once again, possibly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite willing to assist. Do I understand well that at the earlier occasion where I read it, it has understandably and for a good purpose not been translated, since I was quoting the original? So if that is now true, would you now translate it into B/C/S. It reads, "UkrBat, during the reported period the situation was relatively tense due to SA fire and RT shelling in the vicinity of Tito barracks." It has been translated to you, Mr. Halili?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it has, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, and it is merely for the record, can you confirm that this is a document which originated with the UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. Again, there's no proper foundation for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just ask a different -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is there any difference in view between the parties whether this is a UN document or not? If you could compromise on the UN source, which it seems to me that you take the position that this might be a UN document. If there's no defensive view, we could just establish that the parties agree upon the source of this document. And looking to you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is that what you want to establish as the first part of your ... I mean, I'm not going into the content, just about the source.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Shall I answer now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm trying to find out if there's any dispute about the source of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, there are objections, but there is no dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, since I'm at this moment interfering, I just want to know the relevance of the questioning and the relevance of the questioning totally depends on whether there's any dispute on the source of this document. Your questioning gave me the impression that you're seeking to establish that it was a UN document. If that's not true, please tell me.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my objective was to establish what exactly do we have here coming from the United Nations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the first question was the source of the document. I'm not going to have a conference over --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- of the document. This document was disclosed by the Prosecution and the source of the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking the Defence, and for the first time I ask you to say yes or no: Do you seek to establish that this is a UN document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is there any dispute as far as the source of the document is concerned?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed. This is according to the compromise of the parties a UN document. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, before I was interrupted, I was about to ask you the following, and I return again to the document which came from the United Nations UNPROFOR. Have you now understood the sentence which was interpreted for you by the interpretation service of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Again an objection, Your Honour. The Defence has not raised or set forth a proper foundation whether this witness has even seen an UNPROFOR sitrep before, nor whether he has any type of expertise to testify about the terminology used in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you, before putting this question to the witness, please establish, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the basis for any assumption that this witness could interpret UN documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I was not asking for an interpretation of the document. All I asked was that the witness, who said that he could read English, but obviously with difficulty. He said that at first he couldn't understand the interpretation. My simple question was: Did he understand, if he grasped the meaning of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I don't have to explain to you that reading a legal book or a book on chemistry, although you understand perhaps all the words, might give a difference in understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed. That is why I asked that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in this sentence, which you have understood perfectly, we read, in English, that the situation [inaudible]. So my question is: A moment ago you -- at the vicinity of the Marsal Tito barracks, you heard only two bullets, two shots fired. Will you please confirm your earlier statement.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I am confirming it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to move on with -- "came from the United Nations, I see that there was shelling, that is, artillery shelling in that area." Is it that you never heard any shelling in that area on that day?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was no shelling that day. There was a truce that day, a cease-fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for your answer. I'd like to go back to the Tito barracks, which we can see on this photograph. Witness, do you know if in the Tito barracks that you mentioned there were also Bosniak troops?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there were UNPROFOR troops and the BH army troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you just mentioned the BH army. Do you know if in that army there were some sniper units too? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, I don't think so, because UNPROFOR was there. UNPROFOR controlled a larger part of the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the question that I asked you dealt with the BH army, as you said, not necessarily they saw that unit. My question was of a general nature.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: And I answered you to the best of my knowledge. What I knew, I told you. I never set my foot in these barracks to know how many troops there were, but what I do know for certain is that the UNPROFOR was in there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, I think there's some misunderstanding in questioning and giving your answer. The question was whether in the BiH army, in general, so not just that part of the army that was in the Tito barracks at that time, but generally in the area, in the city, wherever the BiH army was, whether there were any sniper units as a part of this army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So, Witness, you never saw weapons in your army, that is, the BH army, which could be used as sniping weapons?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, are you aware of a factory which was in Sarajevo and which was making optical devices? And if you are aware of that, what was it called?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Believe me, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But I do believe you. And Witness, the name of that factory, Zrak, tells you nothing, rings no bells?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Now that you said it, yes, I've heard about this factory, but what it made, I don't remember. I simply -- I don't know that. Because I came to Sarajevo on the eve of the war, and at that time I didn't really know Sarajevo all that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you think or do you know, do you remember, if that factory, Zrak, was operational during the war?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I'd like to go back to some of your statements. Is it correct to say that you looked through, checked, verified, saw it, a statement on the 10th of November, 1995, a statement talking to the investigators of the International Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring, Mr. President, to a document which we wish to show the witness and then tender. I have before me the Serbian text, which was submitted to the witness. So it is up to you to decide. That is, it has to do with one word in that text, and that word in Serb reads "soliter."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think, if it's just about one word or one line, to put the text in front of the witness, but if you would please read it clearly and indicate perhaps prior to reading it to the Prosecution what part you're referring to so that they can follow you. As you know, the Bench has no copies of these statements. And then if it's just about one word, in order to avoid whatever misunderstanding as far as the translation is concerned, if the line has been read, I'd invite the Prosecution to read the same line in English so to see that there's no problem as far as translation is concerned. Please proceed -- please indicate first, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, where you're referring to, what page of the document, whether it's in the middle or ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interpreters do not have copies of this text, so could it be read very slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is 0096461. The statement is in Serbian. On the 10th of November, 1995. Mr. President, may I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The number you gave, is that the number of the Serbian text?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is the document which we see in the Serbian version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has the Prosecution found the statement we are talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] ERN.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has been found. Is this a one-page document or are there more pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As usual, there are several pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the middle --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We're afraid we could not hear the exact line because the counsel were speaking over the President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you indicate approximately at what line, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, it is 365, in the middle of the eighth line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You found it, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but if I could, briefly, for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The ERN number is slightly different from that reflected on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we'll read the text anyhow, so the ERN number is not of major importance at this moment. Could you please then read slowly for the interpretation the lines you want to refer to, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be happy to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, with regard to this statement which I have before my eyes, you spoke about shots coming from what was defined a moment ago as a white skyscraper. You indicated that these shots came - and I'm quoting, now I'm reading - "from the first floor." Can you confirm the statement to us?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I told them I think from somewhere between the first and the tenth floor. What they noted down, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, your statement, did you sign it in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I suppose I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And is it true that in Serbian you use those two words, sa provog sprata, the first floor, which I have before me?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: What I said was it could be between the first and the tenth floor that the shots came from, because I couldn't go there to see them, to look at them. Those were purely guesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I shall move on to another question, Mr. President. You told us that the front lines were very near the place where this unfortunate accident happened, that is, the river concerned. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: The separation line was nearby, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did it happen that around that line the fighting would break out?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, yes, there would be gunfire time and again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And Witness, this gunfire which you mentioned, was it an exception along the front line or, lamentably, the rule?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, there would be gunfire, I mean, serving no particular purpose. There would just be shots fired.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to your knowledge, the two armies, or the two parties, did they confront one another on that line on the day of the incident too?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I'm not -- I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I shall rephrase my question. I'm sorry. To your knowledge, on the day of the incident, did the -- the front line was the same, unchanged?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, no, not that, but they also said that there was a ceasefire. It was a quieter day. I said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what truce, what cease-fire did they have that day?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Not to open fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told that there was a cease-fire -- between whom and whom?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, looking at the clock, you asked us when we would have a break. I said at 12.30. We are a few minutes past. Would you find a suitable moment to interrupt your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, I shall resume after the break, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So Mr. Halili, we'll have a break for 20 minutes. We'll resume at 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I'm reminding you on the time limits as well. Would you please proceed in your cross-examination of the witness, Mr. Halili.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I will be as brief as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just before the cross-examination resumes, I would be grateful for a moment of the Trial Chamber's time before we adjourn at 1.45. I have something to say. It will not take long. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A couple of minutes would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: More than sufficient, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Before the break, sir, you told us that there was a truce, or a cease-fire. At least, that is what I can see in the English transcript. Who were the signatories of this cease-fire, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Whoever was in charge of signing such an agreement. The international army. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I should like to know between which parties and not which signatories, Witness. That is, to the best of your knowledge, who signed this cease-fire agreement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, the BH army and the former Serb army, the army of this Serb republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, when you say "the former Serb army," what exactly do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, I mean their army, the one that they had during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I should like the witness to be shown a map. We have a map here, but it was premarked by the wife of the witness during the interview with her. We can see -- we can show the witness that map or the other one which is in the possession of the Registry. It's up to you. The map in question is 02110612, and it is the Prosecution number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you want the witness to mark on it or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in accordance with his answers. But perhaps that even won't be necessary, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So let's then just see whether we could use the map in front of you, because usually we need blank maps or at least maps that are without any confusion as far as the marking is concerned, any pre-marking is concerned. Mr. Usher, would you please ... Prosecution, do you have any objection against the map indicated by the Defence? One of the advantages of this map, of course, is that it's quite detailed as far as the streets are concerned, so that's very attractive, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you could just refresh my memory as to which map we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- I'll just have it shown to you. There's a limited pre-marking on it. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Before we finally decide on whether any markings will be made on this map, it can be shown on the ELMO now. Will it be tendered into evidence perhaps in the near future, or is there any intention to do so?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need a minute to consult, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Meanwhile, perhaps Mr. Mundis could answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution is intending on tendering that document through the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that we will be tendering this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, there is a map in front of you. Can you read what's written on this map? Can you read the map?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Well, I'll do my best too, so there will be two of us. On the map that you have in front of you, could you indicate for us with a pointer, which you can see on the desk in front of you, where the intersection was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In order to avoid whatever misunderstanding, I'd like to have the marking done with a thick marker, because there are already some markings with a thin marker on the map. These are the pre-markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we should perhaps take a different colour than the colour red. I see that the red is the one that the usher has at the moment. Perhaps we should use the black one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, although I would rather stick to black and blue. Perhaps in order to avoid misunderstandings, since there are already some black markings on the map, perhaps as an exception we might use red. But Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it would be far easier to start with a blank map and not with all kind of markings on it already, although I do know that the Prosecution did the same now and then. I have to invite both parties to avoid whatever confusion there ever might exist. But we can now use the red marker for marking at trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence will be mindful of that in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, could you please indicate for us the intersection where the incident in question took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may mark it with a red pen.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: To be quite frank, I'm not sure. I'm not very good at reading maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you think you can't do it because you're not -- your ability to read maps is not sufficiently developed, then please tell us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, could you please indicate for us - that's going to be easier perhaps - the location of the Marsal Tito barracks on this map.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly where it is. I'm more than willing to do it, but I don't think I can. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It seems to me, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, that the witness has some difficulties in map-reading, so would you please keep that in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm trying too, but I'm also trying to elicit as precise questions as possible and discuss the facts as they are. I now have to rephrase my questions, because the witness obviously has some difficulties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you have a look at the map and see where the area of Hrasno is located. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you now please indicate on the map the location.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Could you please now circle the area called Hrasno on this map.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you also indicate for us, sir, since you told us you were a soldier, which was the brigade that you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, could you please repeat your answer. The interpreters were not able to hear you.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I belonged to the 101st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, could you tell us if the headquarters of the 101st Brigade were located close to the circle that you have just made on the map, that is, close to the area of Hrasno?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: There was a battalion located in Hrasno.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. And now, in order to clarify the matters, could you tell us now how many people usually a battalion consists? What is the strength of a battalion, in terms of manpower?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: About 40 people, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are referring to soldiers with weapons, armed soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, yes, they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question was: Were those soldiers armed soldiers? I'm insisting on this question because the witness told us that there was not enough weapons even for standing guards, so I should like to know whether those soldiers were armed.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: When they were on guard duty, they probably had weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just looking at the transcript, you started your question with whether there was a battalion -- whether there was headquarters of the 101st Brigade located close to the circle indicated. The answer was that there was a battalion located in Hrasno. Then you asked about the general strength of a battalion and then you continued about whether the soldiers were armed. Are you referring to soldiers located in Hrasno or -- the questioning is not quite clear to me, so it might confuse the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. President. For the moment, I am discussing Hrasno, that is, the battalion that the witness has told us about, which consisted of 40 persons. I'm talking about them at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So the question, Mr. Halili, is about whether the 40 soldiers -- you didn't say Hrasno, but you said the general strength of a battalion was 40 people. And now the question is whether any 40 people in Hrasno were armed or not.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: When they were on guard duty, they had weapons, but generally speaking, there was not enough weaponry for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. Does that mean that there were soldiers who were incorporated in the unit but did not carry weapons because there were not enough weapons? Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answer. How about yourself, sir, since you were also a soldier? Did you have a weapon or not?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: When I was on guard duty, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And when you would finish your shift, your guard duty, what would happen with your personal weapon? What would you do with it?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I did not have my personal weapon. I was issued with an automatic rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say "personal" -- when I say "weapon," and when you say "personal weapon," I am not referring to a weapon that you may have owned personally, but something that you carried at the moment. So I should like to know what would happen with that automatic rifle that you had been issued with.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Well, the others would take it over.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, while you were engaged in the army and while you were armed, where would you spend your nights? Where would you sleep?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Usually I would stay at home overnight. That's where I would spend the night, because I lived close to the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You were therefore a military man who was engaged; however, in the evening you would return home to your personal dwelling. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, in most of the cases, because the conditions were very bad in terms of sleeping.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Witness. Could you now indicate, if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. possible, on the map where your residence was.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: It is situated on Trg Heroje Square.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you indicate the location on the map, Witness, so that we can see what the distance was.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm afraid I haven't seen the location. Could you mark it with a different sign, that is, your place of residence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You could perhaps put a second circle on the location in question.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Witness, while you were active in the army, where exactly was the command of the battalion? I'm referring to the battalion to which you belonged.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: It was located in one of the skyscrapers. There are five skyscrapers on the square, and we were located in the cellar of one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. When you were on duty in the battalion, did you wear a uniform; and if so, what kind?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: I did not wear any uniform, because we didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But you were engaged in this battalion; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And when you carried your weapon, you had no uniform either?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, for your answer. As regards the weaponry which was available to this battalion - and I am referring to the year 1993 - what exactly did you have? I heard you speak about a machine-gun, and I should like to know what other types of weapon you had at the battalion.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: We had five rifles for the entire guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what would happen with other soldiers, those who were with you on duty and who did not have any weapons? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: They were undergoing some sort of preparations or training.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you participate in any military engagement?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Do you meanwhile I was a soldier in the army?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: With this battalion?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So if I understand you correctly, there were only five of you.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: But there would be five of us who were on guard duty, on Trg Heroje Square.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to participate in a military operation is not the same thing as to stand guard, to be on guard duty. You said that there were only five of you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you're using the word "engagement" the first time and you're now using "operation militaire." That is not the same wording with, and since you're confronting the witness with his answer, I'd like you to mind again the way you put your questions to the witness and not to --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You seem all right here as following part of the French. You're creating confusion, and I'll not allow you to do so. I'll ask the witness now to explain exactly what he meant by engaging in, I would say, military activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Halili, when you are talking about your -- and let me just read it literally. I just have to find it. The question was put to you: "Did you participate in any military engagement?" Your answer then was: "Do you mean while I was a soldier in the army?" Then Mr. Piletta-Zanin had said yes, and then you said: "Yes, I did." So you did participate in a military engagement. Could you explain to us, apart from being on guard, as you testified before, what else would be this military engagement, if anything else.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I understand what you mean. I never took part in any action. I stood guard. I was on guard duty, but I never participated in any action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other action than being a guard; do I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I don't think I'm teaching anyone, but perhaps finding clear answers presupposes that there are clear questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I will bear that in mind, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You told us, sir - and it was marked by a red circle - that there was a skyscraper on a photograph that I don't know the number because you -- because it was erased, but this is a document which I would like shown again, Mr. President, shown to the witness. The Prosecution seem to have erased the number. I don't know what the number is, but it's 02114267?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 466, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is only one number. There is only one number on this document that I am holding. It is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's a red stricken out and there's a black number on it and we discussed the different numbering. So that's 02114266 you're indicating to. That's the picture that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is a document which was submitted, but I did not finish. This was submitted and shown to the witness during his examination-in-chief, and I can see only one number, and I believe there is a letter. It was stricken, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... two different versions around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have it here on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I please have the photo -- the copy you've got in your hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to be absolutely certain that this is the very same photograph that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know who provided this copy to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I do agree with you that there's just the red number on it, so I'm glad that I verified it. I don't know whether a copy without a black number has ever been provided to the Defence, which of course would create a lot of confusion, having two numbers on it, one stricken out, another one, a black one, on top, not on the copy which is available to the Defence at this moment. That's really confusing. It takes us a lot of time and I don't need any comment apart from that you understood what I mean. Is there any additional copy available for the Defence? Mr. Piletta-Zanin, of course I wanted to verify whether you -- you see on the screen now that there are two numbers. That's the copy we have. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Thank you. I wanted to be absolutely certain that we're talking about the same photograph, and now, thanks to you, it is all clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to have a look at this photograph on your right, and I believe mine is the very same picture except for a different number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I please ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, because I want to have these kind of things clarified: Has, during the examination-in-chief, another copy, the copy used while examining the witness, has that also been provided to the Defence? That's the copy with the two numbers on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I know, I don't think so. I don't see -- I only see one copy. I don't see the other one was provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was informed that the usher did give to the Defence also a copy with the red stricken-out number and the black number. Yes. Would you --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it's here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please refrain from saying about just one number on your copy when a couple of minutes ago not only the double-numbered copy has been given to you, but apart the from that, I indicated that there were two numbers on it. So at that moment you would have been able to concentrate on the copy provided to you at that very moment and not make any fuss about an earlier copy. Because that's the copy you are now providing to the witness, not the one-numbered copy, not the bad copy, but the two-numbered copy. Please proceed. Which copy is now in front of the witness? Is that the -- I am putting a question. I want to be sure what copy is on the ELMO. That's the double-numbered copy, as far as I understand. Okay. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I truly apologise. I am sorry. This was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- our mistake. Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No other questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Is there any need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Has any of my colleagues any additional questions? Judge Nieto-Navia will put questions to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes. I would like the diagram to be put there, the first diagram we saw. Would you please indicate the direction, according to your opinion, of the bullet, there.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: From this direction, on the left-hand side, this arrow here on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: So the bullet went through the containers, through the -- or through the trailer?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes. It ricocheted from the asphalt, and that's when it hit her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also have a question for you, Mr. Halili. You told us that your mother moved to the post office building and would sleep there. Could you please tell us where she lived before she moved to the post office building.

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: It was on the Hero Square. That was former street Pero Kosoric, on the 19th floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you indicate Hero Square, in which part of the city that is?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: In Hrasno. That is the name of the part of the town, Hrasno, and the street is Hero Square, or Trg Heroje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you explain to us exactly why she felt it was dangerous to stay there and move to the post office building?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Because every morning she had to go to work, and there was a bridge that was very, very dangerous. There was shooting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would this mean that she would have to cross the river, the Miljacka River?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And because of the dangerousness of the crossing, she decided then to live at the other side of the river, I understand. Apart from sleeping in the post office building, where would she stay when she was not working, when she was not sleeping?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: While she was working, and then when she would finish her shift, she was there the whole time in the post office building. Sometimes I would go and get her to the post office and then we would go together to the apartment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were there other people that had moved into this post office building in a similar way as your mother-in-law did?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Yes. There were people who were refugees, who had escaped, and there were other people as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you tell us the approximate number of people that were just, I would say, residing in the post office building?

utterances.speaker: SABRI HALILI
utterances.text: Once I went into the cellar of the building, and there were over 180 people in the post office building, in the cellar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. Mr. Halili, this is the end of your examination in this courtroom. Both parties and the Judges have put questions to you. You'll understand it's important for the Chamber to get information which might help them in taking decisions we'll have to take. We thank you very much for coming this very far way to The Hague, and I wish you a good journey home again. Thank you. Mr. Usher, would you please lead Mr. Halili out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, unless you would indicate otherwise to me, I'd suggest that once we finish the admittance into evidence of whatever documents presented for this witness, it's of no use to call the next witness, and perhaps we might use the five minutes then remaining to give you an opportunity t bring whatever -- Ms. Pilipovic, I was just looking too much to the left.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you'll allow me, I have just one comment -- the Defence has one comment, and one of the problems that we have in our work. We have 15 photographs in this particular case, and that is the problem why there is sometimes a problem in communication. And perhaps our colleagues could accept this. And if they can refrain from giving us so many photographs, so much material, because that is taking a lot of our time, and we find very difficult to tell one photograph from the other, and there are many numbers. And I understand that we should just take into account these photographs that we are given by the Registry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with you to the extent that the Chamber has it far easier, because photographs are only presented during trial. So there's no risk of confusing similar photographs -- the photographs provided before. On the other hand, I'd like very much to concentrate that whenever a document is shown to a witness, we should on from that moment concentrate on that document, because that document will be tendered into evidence. And I have understanding for the problems the Defence is facing, and as you might have noticed, apart from some strong words now and then in the direction of the Defence, I similarly address the Prosecution when I thought they could perform better. So then we'll have the admission into evidence. As far as my recollection goes, we have P3662, a diagram. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps I misheard Your Honour, but the diagram is numbered P3262.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, then I make a mistake. Yes, it's 3662. I apologise for -- Madam Registrar, she always helps us out if it really becomes difficult.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's document P3262.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the diagram. Perhaps I had better leave it to you, Madam Registrar. We have the video shown to the witness, which would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P8 -- I'm sorry. 3280C, 3280C.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we have a set of two photos.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3271.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it's not a matter of admission into evidence, but just for clarity reasons, that the portion shown to this witness of Exhibit 3279A, so the portion shown today is included in the admission into evidence of this 360-degree photograph. And then the final document we have, it starts, I think, with a "P" number, but since it has been tendered by the Defence -- there are two. The first is I think the UN document.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D32, and the portion of the map of Sarajevo, D33.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So then all these documents are admitted into evidence. Mr. Ierace or Mr. Mundis, you still had something.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President and Your Honours, this morning I received a letter by facsimile from my learned friend Mr. Stephane Piletta-Zanin. It was in the French language, so I took some steps to have it translated. I received that translation immediately before we recommenced this last session, and shortly after, I had arranged with my learned friend a meeting to take place tomorrow afternoon at 2.00, being the weekly meeting that you, Mr. President, have requested us to engage in so that we can sort out any admissibility problems and so shorten time unnecessarily taken in Court. Mr. President, I have read the translation, and it seems that it is a letter that was copied to some other individuals, including the Senior Legal Officer, Mr. Fourmy. I do not know whether Your Honours and you, Mr. President, have had an opportunity yet to read the letter. It raises two issues, one directly. I'll wait until you indicate to me that you have read it, and I seek your guidance as to whether you wish me to respond; and if so, whether you wish me to do so orally or in writing or both. I will be happy to do so. The second issue it raises is an indirect one.
