Suffice to say, until Your Honours and you, Mr. President, have had an opportunity to read and consider the letter, it could be fairly said that it raises a serious concern as to whether the meetings which you wish to take place can productively take place without there being present either the Senior Legal Officer or a representative to ensure that what transpires in those meetings is accurately reflected in the Trial Chamber. I regret to have to say that, but having read the letter, there seems no alternative. Mr. President and Your Honours, until such time as you have an opportunity to respond, it is probably, unfortunately, necessary that the meeting tomorrow does not go ahead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am not aware of having received a letter or a copy of a letter. Since this letter has been raised in Court and since I noticed that there has some difference of view as far as what has been said during a meeting outside of Court was pointed at by the parties, I wonder whether the parties -- I don't know whether the letter is addressed to us or whether the parties want to provide us with a copy. Because since I do not know the content, I do not know whether any intervention from the Chamber would be appropriate or not. So I'm not aware of any letter. No copy, as far as I know, was on my desk.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the letter was addressed to me and it was marked as having been copied to various individuals in the Tribunal, including Mr. Fourmy. I hesitate to inform Your Honours of the content of the letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I would prefer that you initially read it privately. I do not have the original with me. It is with the member of our team who translated it for me. I would be content to wait until tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we could do that best. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the letter to which refers Mr. Ierace is -- a copy has been sent to Mr. Fourmy. Do I understand that it was your intention that Mr. Fourmy would communicate the content of the letter with the Chamber or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, am I allowed to respond very briefly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was my intention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was your intention. So then I'll take care that we -- the Chamber will read the letter this afternoon and we'll then see whether it's appropriate to discuss the letter in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps since Mr. Ierace was -- took some time in expressing this, I was -- may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What happened is that I worked on a number of continents, in a number of jurisdictions, whether they were arbitrary, civilian, or criminal, and this has been going on for some 20 years, or even a quarter of a century. It never happened during the entire time, without any false modesty, that any magistrate put words in my mouth that I have not spoken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I asked you yesterday whether the misquoting was something you wanted to be investigated by this Chamber or not, or that you just would like to have it corrected during the oral hearing, and you said that was what you wanted at this moment. I can tell you that I went through the transcript to locate precisely the remark you referred to. So if you now want to -- if you have now changed your mind -- I wouldn't mind. If you say, "No. It's a matter that really needs some further investigation," that's fine, but I offered you to dive into the matter. You said it was not necessary. Do I understand you well that now you want us to deal with it, or -- because you are now -- perhaps it's some justification. I don't know. You're now complaining about what happened, being misquoted for something you said outside of Court. I'd like to be -- first of all, I would like to clarify on whether you want the Chamber to be -- to deal with the matter or not, because yesterday you said that it was not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, thank you so much for that intervention. Yesterday -- I said yesterday it was useless for the Trial Chamber to use -- to waste time, and that this could be dealt with directly. And that is the reason why I addressed a direct letter to Mr. Ierace, and perhaps he did not accept it - this was just a European courtesy- that I copy that letter to a number of people. And I was hoping that this problem could be resolved like that. However, if I am being misquoted, told that I said things which I didn't, and then I would like Mr. Ierace to take the consequences. I would never -- I do not want to have people to say words that I did not say. If Mr. Ierace thinks that we can deal with it outside of the Chamber, then that is fine; but if the Trial Chamber wants to deal with it, that is fine, but not me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. What we'll do is we'll read the letter and we'll find a solution one way or the other that the parties continue to communicate with each other. If not, of course this will have consequences on how this trial will be held. We'll give it proper reflection. We'll then adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 31st day of January, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 9.52 a.m.,
